newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. delegation in Beijing to discuss human rights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. delegation in Beijing to discuss human rights.

text.p: A U.S. delegation is visiting China for talks on human rights with Chinese officials after a year that saw the imprisonment or exile of virtually every political dissident, a U.S. official said on Wednesday.
The delegation, which arrived in Beijing on Tuesday, would hold talks over the next two days with Chinese officials, a U.S. embassy official said.
"They will discuss a broad range of bilateral issues and it will include human rights," said the official, who declined to be identified.
The U.S. team arrived in China on the eve of the release of Washington's annual worldwide human rights report that once again slams Beijing's record.
This year's report says that by the end of 1996, there were no active dissidents left in China who had not been jailed or exiled, U.S. officials said on Tuesday.

Officials said the team would seek concessions from Beijing on human rights that could make it unneccessary this year for Washington to co-sponsor a United Nations resolution critical of China's policy.
But Washington was still prepared to support the resolution this year if Beijing showed no improvement in its protection of fundamental freedoms, the embassy official said.

"They've told the Chinese many times that unless there is progress on human rights issues of international concern, the U.S. is prepared to co-sponsor a resolution on China at the U.N. human rights commission," he said.

China has angrily fought passage of the annual U.N. resolution, saying it constitutes interference in its internal affairs. Beijing succeeded in quashing the resolution last April for the sixth year in a row.

The U.S. delegation was led by Sandra Kristoff, the National Security Council's chief Asia expert, and included Peter Eicher, director of the State Department's Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights and Labour, the embassy official said.
